name: Boost decomposition of (U, Gamma) as standard Misner-Sharp-Hernandez kinematics

source.located: W. C. Hernandez & C. W. Misner, ApJ 143, 452 (1966) 'Observer time as a coordinate in relativistic spherical hydrodynamics' and C. W. Misner & D. H. Sharp, Phys. Rev. 136, B571 (1964) -- neither on arXiv. The 'Misner-Sharp-Hernandez' formalism read via three arXiv restatements: A. Helou, I. Musco & J. C. Miller, arXiv:1601.05109v6 (CQG 34, 135012, 2017) pp.3-6, 8-11, 30 (footnote p.3: 'This formalism (using a diagonal metric) was first presented by Misner & Sharp [24] and then re-expressed with extended terminology in a paper by Hernandez & Misner [25] ... What we describe here as the "Misner-Sharp-Hernandez" approach is, in fact, a composite' of MS 1964, HM 1966 and May & White 1966); V. Faraoni, G. F. R. Ellis, J. T. Firouzjaee, A. Helou & I. Musco, arXiv:1610.05822 (PRD 95, 024008, 2017) pp.5-8, 12-13; A. Escriva, arXiv:2504.05813v3 (2025) pp.3-5, 12. Invariance cross-read in S. A. Hayward, arXiv:gr-qc/9408002v2 (PRD 53, 1938, 1996) pp.3-4, 16.
source.via: alphaXiv answer_pdf_queries on 1601.05109, 1610.05822, 2504.05813, gr-qc/9408002, 2601.03077. Hernandez & Misner 1966 and Misner & Sharp 1964 themselves NAMED-NOT-READ. The explicit two-observer boost U' = cosh w U + sinh w Gamma, Gamma' = sinh w U + cosh w Gamma was NOT found verbatim in any source read; what the restatements print is (i) the definitions U = D_t R, Gamma = D_r R in the fluid's comoving frame, (ii) Gamma^2 - U^2 = grad R . grad R = 1 - 2M/R, (iii) HMM eq.(15) dR/dtau = U + Gamma v for an object moving at 3-velocity v relative to the fluid, and (iv) Faraoni eqs.(4.16)-(4.17), the comoving-vs-Kodama relative Lorentz factor 1/sqrt(1 - U^2/Gamma^2), |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|. The boost form follows from (iii) by time dilation in two lines (re-derived here, check C1).

published_statement: Helou-Musco-Miller 1601.05109 p.5, eqs.(3)-(6): 'In the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez approach, two basic differential operators are introduced D_t = (1/a) d/dt and D_r = (1/b) d/dr, representing derivatives with respect to proper time and radial proper distance in the comoving frame of the fluid ... U = D_t R ... Gamma = D_r R, with U being the radial component of four-velocity in an "Eulerian" (non comoving) frame where R is used as the radial coordinate, and Gamma being a generalized Lorentz factor ... related to the Misner-Sharp-Hernandez mass M ... by the constraint equation Gamma^2 = 1 + U^2 - 2M/R'; p.5-6 eq.(9): 'M = (R/2)(1 - grad_a R grad^a R) with grad_a R grad^a R = Gamma^2 - U^2'. p.8 eq.(15)-(16): '(1/a) dR/dt = dR/dtau = (U + Gamma v), where v = (b/a) dr/dt is the 3-velocity of the object whose worldline is being considered, measured with respect to the local comoving frame of the fluid.' Faraoni et al 1610.05822 p.5: 'the areal radius R is a geometric quantity which is independent of the foliation ... all spherically symmetric foliations will produce the same apparent horizons (but this is not true of non-spherical foliations)'; 'in spherical symmetry [the Hawking mass] becomes gauge-independent because it is defined by the scalar equation (3.1)'; p.12-13 eqs.(4.16)-(4.17): 'u^a_(K) u_(C)a = -1/sqrt(1 - U^2/Gamma^2) = -gamma(v_rel) ... |v_rel| = |U/Gamma|'. Hayward gr-qc/9408002 p.3: 'One may also use one spatial and one temporal direction ... but there is no unique choice of such directions'; p.4: 'Note that E is an invariant.'
published_hypotheses: spherical symmetry of the spacetime (HMM p.4: 'we work entirely within spherical symmetry for both the spacetime and the trapped surfaces'; Hayward p.2)

MSH setting: diagonal 'cosmic time' metric ds^2 = -a^2 dt^2 + b^2 dr^2 + R^2 dOmega^2 with r comoving with the fluid, u^a = (1/a,0,0,0) -- the orthogonal comoving foliation (HMM eq.2 p.4-5; Escriva eq.2.2 p.3)

matter: perfect fluid T = (e+p) u u + p g (HMM eq.7; Escriva eq.2.1); needed for the MSH evolution equations and for M = int 4 pi R^2 e dR, NOT for the kinematic identity Gamma^2 - U^2 = grad R . grad R
'a, b and R are positive definite functions of r and t' (HMM p.5); Gamma's sign not fixed there, and Escriva p.12 reports Gamma < 0 realised in type-II (non-monotonic R) data
foliation-independence of grad R . grad R holds only for spherically symmetric foliations (Faraoni p.5)
HMM eq.(15): tau is the COMOVING proper time; U + Gamma v is dR per comoving proper time, not per the moving object's proper time
hypothesis_drift: BROADENED, and supported: MSH defines U, Gamma in the fluid's comoving frame with a perfect fluid (HMM p.5, Escriva p.3); foliation.py:108-116,128-134 applies them to ANY spherically symmetric unit timelike u with no matter model. Supported: the boost and the invariant are metric-only identities -- re-derived here for free Phi, Lambda, R, w (checks A1-A9) and for a general 2-metric with shift (B1-B4); no field equation enters. Hayward p.3-4 and Faraoni p.5 say the same in words.

KEPT: restriction to spherically symmetric foliations (Faraoni p.5). foliation.py:110 'spherically symmetric unit timelike field' carries it; the tree's 'every foliation' (foliation.py:145-148) means every SPHERICALLY SYMMETRIC foliation, and the prose does not repeat the qualifier at :145-148 or in GAMMA_RANGE (foliation.py:856) and INVARIANT_CRITERION (foliation.py:858).

DROPPED IN PROSE, KEPT IN z3 (tree-side, affects downstream corollaries, not the boost itself): orientation of n such that Gamma > 0. foliation.py:140-148 ('THE ACHIEVABLE SET IS Gamma in [k, infinity)'; 'GAMMA > 1 IN EVERY FOLIATION <=> m < 0') and the status string GAMMA_RANGE (foliation.py:856) and INVARIANT_CRITERION (foliation.py:858) state no orientation; the z3 obligations carry G > 0 (foliation.py:790, 809, 812, 843-844) and the O12 prose names it once (foliation.py:156). With n reversed the same geometry has Gamma in (-inf, -k] and 'Gamma > 1 in every foliation' fails at m < 0 (check F2, computed); |Gamma| > 1 survives (F3). An orthochronous boost cannot change the sign of Gamma on the untrapped branch (E6, z3 unsat), so the orientation is a fixed choice, and Escriva p.12 shows Gamma < 0 is realised in the literature's own data.
KEPT: orthochronous boosts only (cosh w > 0); z3 carries c > 0 (foliation.py:798-799). Time reversal would flip U only.

The ingredients (U, Gamma definitions; Gamma^2 - U^2 = 1 - 2m/R; dR/dtau = U + Gamma v) are MSH and READ here via restatement; the cosh/sinh two-observer boost as a formula was not found in any source read -- it is special-relativistic kinematics of the covector dR in the 2-D normal plane, obtained from HMM eq.(15) plus time dilation (C1). foliation.py:383-387 already disclaims novelty for every line of mathematics, and driven.py:70-71 records Hernandez & Misner 1966 as NOT CONSULTED; that record still holds.

Computed counterexample to the orientation-free prose: m = -1, R = 10, n inward gives Gamma = -sqrt(1.2) cosh psi < 1 on every foliation (F2, wanted False), while |Gamma| > 1 holds (F3). Confirms U = D_t R, Gamma = D_r R, Gamma = sqrt(1 + U^2 - 2M/R) (eqs.2.3, 2.5) in comoving gauge; and reports Gamma < 0 realised in type-II (non-monotonic areal radius) data (pp.5, 12), which is the orientation case the tree's prose range 'Gamma in [k, inf)' leaves unnamed. Narrows the tree's downstream prose, not the boost.
E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)) is an invariant; 'there is no unique choice' of spatial/temporal directions (p.3), so frame components of dr are frame-dependent while their Lorentzian norm is not.

Frame changes between foliation-adapted frames on the 2-D normal plane in general spherically symmetric spacetimes (sec.4.1, eqs.64-71), including non-spacelike slices via rigging; the orthonormal boost is the timelike-slice special case. Found by the one discover_papers call; nothing found that contradicts the boost decomposition.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result: Misner & Sharp (1964) and Hernandez & Misner (1966) used no measured datum here -- U, Gamma and the constraint are definitions plus algebra on a spherically symmetric metric, and the boost is special-relativistic kinematics of the covector dR. Evidence that later data cannot move it: the identity is re-derived for ARBITRARY metric functions Phi, Lambda, R and an arbitrary rapidity field w(t,r) (A1-A9), in a gauge with shift (B1-B4), and numerically over 2000 random states (N1); no field equation, equation of state or constant enters. What the authors did not have is not data but scope: they stated it in the comoving frame of a perfect fluid, and the tree uses it for any spherically symmetric observer -- a broadening that the re-derivation supports. The only places where something could 'move' are the tree's own framing: the Gamma > 0 orientation the prose omits (computed counterexample F2), and the docstring sign at foliation.py:129. Neither is a defect of the external result, and neither is caused by missing data.
grade_evidence: The boost decomposition as the tree prints it (foliation.py:132-134) is re-derived exactly in sympy for a free rapidity w(t,r) and free metric functions, and again with a shift (31/31 checks, exit 0); z3 proves the transitivity the tree builds on (E4, unsat, vacuity-guarded). The MSH ingredients are READ via restatement (HMM 1601.05109 eqs.4-6, 9, 15; Faraoni 1610.05822 p.5 and eqs.4.16-4.17; Escriva 2504.05813 eqs.2.3, 2.5), and the boost follows from HMM eq.(15) by time dilation (C1). The tree's broadening from the fluid comoving frame to any spherically symmetric observer is supported because no matter model or field equation enters. No numerical datum is involved. Recorded, not repaired, and none of it changes the grade: (a) the cosh/sinh boost form is not printed verbatim in any MSH source read -- 'standard MSH kinematics' is accurate for the ingredients, and the formula itself is elementary special relativity; (b) the tree's prose range and biconditional (foliation.py:140-148, 856, 858) drop the Gamma > 0 orientation that its z3 carries (foliation.py:790, 843), and a computed inward-n state with m < 0 breaks the prose form (F2), while |Gamma| survives; (c) the docstring sign discrepancy at foliation.py:129 against the code at :635/:649 and HMM eq.(4). Hernandez & Misner 1966 and Misner & Sharp 1964 stay NAMED-NOT-READ.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: finding that the tree's downstream use (ledger D2, specthm fact D2 / class K0 / requirement R1) applies 'Gamma > 1 in every foliation <=> m < 0' where n points inward or Gamma < 0 (for example across a wormhole throat with one radial coordinate running mouth to mouth). The boost would then hold, but the corollary would be used on a class its hypothesis (Gamma > 0) excludes. Also to NARROWED: a use with non-spherically-symmetric foliations, where Faraoni p.5 shows the invariance claim fails.
